adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — A rolling deployment mixes legacy SET keys with ZADD/ZCARD calls, causing WRONGTYPE errors and aborting span batches until the old keys expire.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a migration from Redis SET operations (sadd, scard, sscan) to SORTED SET operations (zadd, zcard, zscan) in buffer.py. During a rolling deployment, old instances would still use SET commands while new instances use SORTED SET commands on the same keys. Redis returns WRONGTYPE errors when you try to use SET commands on a SORTED SET key or vice versa. The code at line 197 changes from `p.sadd(set_key, ...)` to `p.zadd(set_key, ...)`, and the Lua script also changes from sunionstore/scard to zunionstore/zcard. If old and new code run simultaneously against the same Redis keys, this will cause WRONGTYPE errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Reducing redirect traversal from 10000 to 1000 silently fragments traces whose parent chain exceeds 1000 spans.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the loop limit being reduced from 10000 to 1000 at line 30. The original comment stated 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1000, traces with parent chains exceeding 1000 levels would now be affected. However, this is more of a design/architecture concern than a bug - the original code already had this limitation at 10000, and the change is intentional (likely for performance). The finding correctly identifies a behavioral change that could affect deep traces, but whether this is a 'bug' depends on whether such deep traces exist in practice. This is a legitimate concern about the scope of the change rather than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — Score-only eviction can discard a root span when it has the earliest end timestamp, leaving the queued segment marked rooted but flushing no root span.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that spans are now stored in sorted sets (ZADD) with end_timestamp_precise as the score, and when span_count > 1000, the code uses 'zpopmin' to evict spans with the lowest scores (earliest end timestamps). The 'has_root_span' flag is set based on whether a root span was ever added to the set, but if the root span happens to have the earliest end_timestamp_precise, it could be evicted by zpopmin while the has_root_span flag remains true. This would result in a segment marked as having a root span but actually missing it when flushed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:839 — OptimizedCursorPaginator applies math.floor/ceil directly to AuditLogEntry.datetime, so any opted-in nonempty audit-log response raises TypeError.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() at line 839 does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` then `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))`. When used with AuditLogEntry (ordered by '-datetime'), self.key would be 'datetime', and the value would be a datetime object. Calling math.floor() or math.ceil() on a datetime object raises TypeError. The endpoint at organization_auditlogs.py uses this paginator with order_by='-datetime', so any non-empty audit log response would fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Writing ZADD to existing span buffer Set keys causes WRONGTYPE failures for live pre-deploy segments during rollout.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a change from using Redis SET commands (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to SORTED SET commands (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) in buffer.py. During a rolling deployment, some instances will write with the new ZADD command while existing keys in Redis may still be SET type from the old code. Redis will return WRONGTYPE error when trying to execute sorted set commands on keys that are regular sets. This is a real deployment/migration issue - the code doesn't handle the transition between data types for existing keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Reducing redirect traversal from 10,001 to 1,001 hops splits valid deep traces into separate buffers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the loop limit in add-buffer.lua being reduced from 10000 to 1000 (line 30). The original comment stated 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1000, traces with depth between 1001 and 10000 that previously worked will now fail to be joined correctly. This is a real behavioral change that could cause valid deep traces to be split into separate buffers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result instead of isolating the offset policy, creating two pagination implementations that will drift.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OptimizedCursorPaginator (lines 818-912) implements its own complete get_result method that largely duplicates the logic from BasePaginator.get_result (visible in the diff at lines 176-195). Both implementations handle cursor processing, offset calculation, queryset slicing, and result building. The only difference is the negative offset handling in OptimizedCursorPaginator. This is a valid architectural concern - having two parallel implementations that share most logic but differ in one policy will likely drift over time as changes are made to one but not the other. This is a real, specific concern grounded in the diff, but it's a design/maintainability issue rather than a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — The new fixed 1000-span eviction cap is separate from SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans, leaving two unsynchronized limits for the same buffer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a hardcoded limit of 1000 in the Lua script (line 62: `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call('zpopmin', set_key, span_count - 1000)`), while the Python code in buffer.py has a separate `max_segment_spans` configuration parameter (visible in the removed code around line 446-452 that checked `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`). The finding correctly identifies that these are two separate limits that could become unsynchronized - one hardcoded in Lua, one configurable in Python. This is a legitimate architectural concern about the change, though not a bug per se since the Lua limit acts as a safety cap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Deploying the SET-to-ZSET conversion against live span keys causes Redis WRONGTYPE errors and Kafka retries until old keys expire.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a migration from Redis SET commands (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to ZSET commands (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) in buffer.py. The Lua script in add-buffer.lua also changes from SET to ZSET operations. However, there's no migration strategy visible in the diff - existing keys in Redis will still be SETs, and when the new code tries to execute ZSET operations (like zcard, zunionstore) on existing SET keys, Redis will return WRONGTYPE errors. This is a real deployment issue that would cause failures until old SET keys expire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — No test inserts more than 1,000 differently scored spans and verifies that only the newest 1,000 are flushed after eviction.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new span eviction mechanism in add-buffer.lua (lines 55-62) that limits spans to 1000 using zpopmin to remove the oldest entries when count exceeds 1000. This is new, non-trivial logic that affects data retention behavior. The finding correctly identifies that no test in the diff verifies this eviction behavior - the test files only add a few spans at a time and don't test the 1000+ span scenario. This is a legitimate missing test coverage concern for newly added functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — No test covers the optimized-pagination opt-in or its administrator access gate, leaving the new paginator path unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new code path in organization_auditlogs.py (lines 68-82) that enables OptimizedCursorPaginator when 'optimized_pagination=true' query param is set and user is superuser or has global access. This is new nontrivial logic with security implications (access control). Reviewing the test files in the diff, none of them test this endpoint or the new pagination path. The finding correctly identifies that this new feature branch lacks test coverage, which is a legitimate review concern for newly added logic with authorization checks.
